ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ideal comparator circuit. The input signal is connected to the non-inverting terminal “+” of the comparator, the reference voltage Vref = 2 V is connected to the inverting terminal “-”, and the right side is the output terminal. Therefore the condition for the output to be high level is that the input voltage is greater than 2 V. Reasoning: The input is a sine wave with 8 V peak-to-peak value and no DC component, so the peak value is 4 V, and it can be written as Vin = 4 sin(ωt). The comparator output is high level if and only if 4 sin(ωt) > 2, that is, sin(ωt) > 1/2. Within one period from 0 to 2π, this occurs between ωt = π/6 and 5π/6, and the duration angle is 5π/6 - π/6 = 2π/3. The duty cycle is (2π/3)/(2π) = 1/3.

Divide by the full period 2π to get the duty cycle 1/3.

method.method_draft: Interpret the circuit visually as a threshold detector with threshold V_T = 2 V and active-high output because the input is on the non-inverting terminal.
